title: Seller's Disclosure Statement (Customary — Caveat Emptor State)
description: Missouri is a caveat emptor state: no statute requires a general seller property disclosure form for residential resales. However, Missouri common law prohibits fraudulent misrepresentation and silent concealment of material defects the seller knows about and the buyer could not reasonably discover (see e.g. VanBooven v. Smull, 938 S.W.2d 324 (Mo. App. W.D. 1997)). The Missouri REALTORS Seller's Disclosure Statement for Residential Property is the customary form and is expected in virtually all brokered transactions. Completing it accurately is the standard risk-management practice; it does not waive the buyer's duty to inspect.

required_actions.note: Missouri REALTORS Seller's Disclosure Statement for Residential Property — customary, not statutory. Deliver before or with the offer; update if material conditions change before closing.

Caveat emptor does NOT protect against active concealment or fraudulent misrepresentation of known material defects. Statutory exceptions (e.g. methamphetamine production, RSMo §442.606) remain mandatory regardless of this form.

citations: Missouri common law (caveat emptor; fraud and concealment exceptions)
VanBooven v. Smull, 938 S.W.2d 324 (Mo. App. W.D. 1997)

title: Methamphetamine Production Disclosure (Statutory)
description: RSMo §442.606 is Missouri's statutory exception to caveat emptor: if any parcel of real property to be sold, exchanged, or transferred is or was used as a site for methamphetamine production, the seller or transferor MUST disclose that fact in writing to the buyer or transferee, provided the seller had knowledge of the prior production. Disclosure is required regardless of whether anyone involved in the production was ever convicted. This duty applies even though Missouri has no general statutory disclosure form.

required_actions.note: The customary Missouri REALTORS disclosure statement contains a methamphetamine section; if no form is used, a standalone written disclosure to the buyer is still statutorily required when the seller has knowledge.
Written disclosure of known methamphetamine production on the premises, regardless of conviction status of the persons involved (RSMo §442.606).

title: Broker Disclosure Form and Brokerage Relationship Confirmation
description: RSMo §339.770 and Missouri Real Estate Commission rule 20 CSR 2250-8.097 require licensees in residential transactions to provide the MREC-prescribed Broker Disclosure Form at the earliest practicable opportunity during or following the first substantial contact with a seller, landlord, buyer, or tenant who has not yet entered a brokerage relationship — and in any event upon obtaining any personal or financial information or before signing a brokerage service agreement, whichever occurs first. Under 20 CSR 2250-8.096 the brokerage relationship must also be confirmed in writing before the party signs a real estate contract. Missouri recognizes seller's agency, buyer's agency, dual agency, transaction brokerage, and designated agency under RSMo §§339.710-339.860.

required_actions.note: MREC Broker Disclosure Form at first substantial contact; written brokerage relationship confirmation before the first signature on the contract.

title: Title Company Closing State
description: Missouri closings are customarily conducted by title insurance companies and title agencies regulated under the Missouri Title Insurance Act, RSMo Chapter 381. Attorney presence is not required at closing. The title company typically performs the title search, issues the title commitment and policy, holds earnest money or closing funds in escrow per RSMo §381.022/§381.412 fiduciary duties, and records the deed. Practice in the Kansas City metro often splits closing between buyer and seller title companies.

required_actions.note: Confirm good funds and escrow disbursement procedures with the title agency; Missouri imposes fiduciary and escrow accounting duties on title agencies under RSMo Chapter 381.

title: No Real Estate Transfer Tax (Constitutionally Prohibited)
description: Missouri imposes no state or local real estate transfer, deed, or conveyance tax — one of the few states with none. Missouri Constitution Article X, Section 25 (Amendment 3, adopted November 2, 2010) affirmatively prohibits the state, counties, and all political subdivisions from imposing any new tax, including a sales tax, on the sale or transfer of homes or any other real estate. Budget only county recorder of deeds recording fees; no transfer tax return or declaration of value is filed.

required_actions.note: No transfer tax due and no transfer tax form exists; confirm only standard county recording fees on the settlement statement.

title: Hazardous Waste Registry Site Disclosure and DNR Notice
description: Properties listed on Missouri's Registry of Confirmed Abandoned or Uncontrolled Hazardous Waste Disposal Sites (maintained by the Department of Natural Resources under RSMo §260.440) are subject to statutory institutional controls under RSMo §260.465: the seller must notify the buyer of the condition of the site prior to sale, the change of ownership must be reported to the department within thirty days, the deed carries notification of contamination, and the use of the site may not change substantially without written approval of the DNR director.

required_actions.note: Seller must notify the buyer of the registry site condition prior to sale (RSMo §260.465).
Report the change of ownership to DNR within 30 days; substantial change of use requires prior written approval of the director.
